name: Baghdad
fact: Founded in 762 as the Round City of the caliph al-Mansur; seat of the Abbasid caliphs ever since.

name: Basra
fact: The port of Sindbad's voyages, on the joined waters of the Tigris and Euphrates.

name: Mosul
fact: Seat of the Zengid atabegs, facing the ruins of ancient Nineveh across the Tigris.

name: Khuzestan
fact: Famed for the Sasanian weirs and water-mills of Shushtar.

name: Shahrazur
fact: Rugged hill country between Iraq and Persia, held by Kurdish chiefs.

name: Luristan
fact: The Zagros highlands of the Lurs, ruled by their own atabegs.

name: Diyar Bakr
fact: Its black basalt walls are among the mightiest of the age.

name: Kartli
fact: Queen Tamar's capital: Georgia is at the height of its golden age.

name: Imereti
fact: Western Georgia, the old land of Colchis and the Golden Fleece.

name: Ani
fact: The old Armenian capital on its gorge, taken by Georgia's generals in 1199.

name: Arran
fact: Home of the poet Nizami, writing his last romances here.

name: Shirvan
fact: Seat of the Shirvanshahs, grown rich on silk and the Caspian trade.

name: Derbent
fact: The Iron Gate: Sasanian walls run from the mountains into the Caspian Sea.

name: Azerbaijan
fact: A great caravan city at the crossroads to Anatolia and the Caucasus.

name: Ardabil
fact: A highland town under Mount Sabalan, the gateway to the Caspian shore.

name: Nakhchivan
fact: The tomb tower of Momine Khatun, built in 1186 for the wife of Eldiguz, rises over the town.

name: Hamadan
fact: Ancient Ecbatana, summer capital of the Persian kings. Avicenna is buried here.

name: Isfahan
fact: Once the capital of the Great Seljuks, a city of gardens on the Zayandeh river.

name: Rey
fact: One of the oldest cities of Persia, and a great stop on the Silk Road.

name: Qazvin
fact: A frontier town facing the castles of Alamut in the mountains above.

name: Alamut
fact: The Eagle's Nest: a fortress on a rock that no army has ever taken.

name: Gilan
fact: Rain-soaked forests on the Caspian shore, never fully ruled by outsiders.

name: Tabaristan
fact: A forested Caspian coast where the Bavandid princes have ruled since the 7th century.

name: Gorgan
fact: The brick tomb tower of Qabus, built in 1006, still stands near here.

name: Kumis
fact: A waystation on the great road between Rey and Nishapur.

name: Quhistan
fact: Desert castles held by the lords of Alamut.

name: Yazd
fact: A desert city cooled by wind-catchers and fed by underground qanats.

name: Fars
fact: Near the ruins of Persepolis, seat of the Salghurid atabegs.

name: Shabankara
fact: Near the round city of Darabgerd, built by the first Sasanian king.

name: Kerman
fact: On the edge of the Lut, one of the hottest deserts on Earth.

name: Hormuz
fact: A trading port where ships from India, Arabia and China unload.

name: Nishapur
fact: Birthplace of Omar Khayyam, and one of the richest cities of Khorasan.

name: Merv
fact: Some historians think it was the largest city in the world in the 1100s.

name: Sarakhs
fact: A caravan stop on the road from Nishapur to Merv.

name: Nasa
fact: An old Parthian royal seat at the foot of the Kopet Dag.

name: Herat
fact: The pearl of Khorasan, held by the Ghurids since 1175.

name: Balkh
fact: Called the mother of cities, and among the oldest towns of Central Asia.

name: Ghor
fact: Its minaret at Jam, built around 1190, rises 65 metres above a hidden valley.

name: Bamiyan
fact: Giant statues carved into its cliffs watch over the valley.

name: Ghazni
fact: Once the capital of the Ghaznavid empire; now the base of Mu'izz al-Din's campaigns.

name: Kabul
fact: A valley town on the road from Bamiyan down to the Khyber Pass.

name: Kandahar
fact: Legend links its founding to Alexander the Great.

name: Sistan
fact: Land of the legendary hero Rostam, where the Helmand river ends in marshes.

name: Badakhshan
fact: Its mountain mines give lapis lazuli and rubies.

name: Khuttal
fact: Famed for the horses bred in its hills north of the Oxus.

name: Termez
fact: The great crossing of the Oxus between Balkh and Samarkand.

name: Khwarazm
fact: Capital of the Khwarazmshahs on the Oxus delta, rich from the steppe trade.

name: Khiva
fact: An oasis town of the Khwarazm delta, behind thick mud-brick walls.

name: Bukhara
fact: The Kalyan minaret, built in 1127, towers over its markets.

name: Samarkand
fact: The jewel of the Silk Road, where paper was first made west of China.

name: Nasaf
fact: A steppe town on the road south from Samarkand to the Oxus.

name: Ushrusana
fact: The mountain gateway into the Ferghana valley.

name: Shash
fact: Called Chach or Shash; one day it will be known as Tashkent, the stone city.

name: Ferghana
fact: A fertile valley famous since antiquity for its heavenly horses.

name: Otrar
fact: A border town on the Jaxartes, the gate between the steppe and the cities.

name: Jand
fact: A town of the lower Jaxartes where the Seljuk Turks first gathered.

name: Talas
fact: Near here in 751, Abbasid and Tang Chinese armies met at the Battle of Talas.

name: Balasagun
fact: The Gurkhan's capital in the Chu valley; the Burana tower stands nearby.

name: Almaliq
fact: A town of the Ili valley on the northern road to China.

name: Kashgar
fact: Where the northern and southern Silk Roads meet beyond the Pamirs.

name: Khotan
fact: Famous for its white and green jade, and for silk.

name: Kipchak Steppe
fact: The endless grass sea of the Kipchak tribes, who sell horses and soldiers to every power.

name: Saqsin
fact: A trading town in the reeds of the Volga delta.

name: Mangyshlak
fact: A desert peninsula on the Caspian, roamed by Turkmen tribes.

name: Peshawar
fact: Old Purushapura, the gateway to India at the foot of the Khyber Pass.

name: Salt Range
fact: Hills of the Khokhar clans, restless under Ghurid rule.

name: Lahore
fact: Taken by the Ghurids in 1186 from the last Ghaznavid ruler.

name: Multan
fact: Known for its scorching summers and ancient walls; Ghurid since 1175.

name: Lower Sindh
fact: The Indus delta, ruled by the Soomra chiefs.

name: Upper Sindh
fact: A fort town on the Indus below the Kirthar hills.

name: Makran
fact: The desert coast where Alexander's army nearly died of thirst.

name: Turan
fact: Dry mountains between Sindh and Kandahar.

name: Kashmir
fact: A valley ringed by mountains; Kalhana wrote its history, the Rajatarangini, in 1148.

name: Delhi
fact: Taken in 1192 after the second battle of Tarain; Aibak governs it for the Ghurids.

name: Ajmer
fact: The old Chahamana capital, lost after Prithviraj's defeat at Tarain in 1192.

name: Ranthambore
fact: A fortress on a rock above the jungle, held by Prithviraj's son.

name: Gwalior
fact: One of the strongest forts in India, on a sandstone cliff.

name: Kannauj
fact: Once the imperial city of northern India; the Gahadavalas lost it in 1194.

name: Kashi
fact: One of the oldest living cities in the world, on the Ganges.

name: Magadha
fact: The old heartland of the Mauryan and Gupta empires.

name: Bengal
fact: A rich delta of rice and fine muslin, ruled by the Sena kings.

name: Jejakabhukti
fact: Kalinjar, a hilltop fortress that has defied many sieges.

name: Malwa
fact: The Paramara kingdom; King Bhoja made Dhar a city of learning.

name: Gujarat
fact: Its army defeated Mu'izz al-Din at Kasahrada in 1178.

name: Saurashtra
fact: A peninsula of ports, with the old fort of Uparkot.

name: Marwar
fact: Desert forts of the Chahamana clans.

name: Thar
fact: A golden sandstone fort in the Thar desert, founded in 1156.
